thesis: Marvell's price move continues to track the Aug 27 beat-and-raise (data center now 79% of revenue) alongside this week's AI Infra Summit disclosures (Photonic Fabric memory-sharing architecture, a 102 Tbps Ethernet switch) and fresh analyst upgrades (Susquehanna to $265, Piper Sandler to Overweight). The Aug 19 Google chip-supply warrant (up to ~6.4% potential dilution) remains inside the 90-day disclosure window and keeps this at low conviction under our fixed rubric regardless of the momentum, alongside a stretched valuation (P/E above 73x, P/S near 22x) the market hasn't resolved.
invalidation: Google warrant dilution materializes without commensurate revenue growth, or the data-center growth trajectory disclosed at the AI Infra Summit fails to show up in Q3 results

thesis: NVIDIA's move this cycle is driven by a mix of disclosed developments -- the Sept 2 definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face, the Sept 14 CUDA-Q quantum-computing platform expansion, and Groq 3 LPX reaching full production for agentic AI inference -- alongside non-fundamental noise (a Trump-Huang phone call dismissing data-center opposition as a 'hoax'). No single factor is clearly dominant, and the DOJ antitrust inquiry and a reported France antitrust probe remain open-ended with no scheduled ruling date, so this sits at medium rather than high.
invalidation: the Hugging Face acquisition faces regulatory pushback, or Q3 FY2027 guidance (due ~Nov 25) walks back the AI-infrastructure demand story

thesis: AXT's latest move is best explained as mechanical rather than fresh fundamental news: confirmed S&P SmallCap 600 index inclusion effective Sept 21 is driving passive-flow buying, but newly launched 2x leveraged/short ETFs (AXTX/AXTQ) are explicitly cited as amplifying the stock's day-to-day volatility, and a 32.9x price-to-sales ratio is drawing renewed valuation scrutiny after a 33% one-month decline. That technical/mechanical framing, not a new disclosed catalyst, caps this at low conviction under our fixed rubric even though the underlying AI-optics demand story (Lumentum supply deal, Q2 growth) is unchanged.
invalidation: leveraged-ETF-driven volatility subsides without the index-inclusion flow producing a durable re-rating, or Q3 2026 results show the AI-optics demand story stalling

thesis: SK hynix's continued strength reflects a mix of a reported (not yet finalized) exploratory deal with Intel to manufacture memory wafers in the US, a confirmed 40 trillion won buyback-and-cancellation program, and a persistent AI-driven DRAM shortage narrative. The July 2026 $26.5B Nasdaq ADR offering (~2.5% dilution) remains inside the 90-day disclosure window and keeps this at low conviction under our fixed rubric regardless of the demand story; the DRAM price-fixing class action and the CEO breach-of-trust police probe both remain open-ended with no scheduled hearing date, so neither is flagged as active litigation.
invalidation: the Intel wafer-supply talks fail to materialize and DRAM/HBM pricing rolls over, or Q3 2026 earnings (~Oct 27) walk back the supercycle guidance

thesis: Apple is trading near its 52-week high on observable iPhone 18 Pro demand signals -- global ship times of 14 days (Pro) and 18 days (Pro Max), both shorter than the equivalent point in last year's iPhone 17 Pro cycle -- alongside the Sept 1 CEO transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus, part of the company's largest leadership turnover since 2011. The ship-time data is a real but indirect demand proxy rather than a hard disclosed sales figure, and how the new CEO settles in remains an open question, keeping this at medium rather than high.
invalidation: iPhone 18 Pro ship times normalize/lengthen in the coming weeks (signaling demand cooling), or the new CEO transition produces a strategy or guidance shift

thesis: Asana's Sept 3 Q2 FY2027 results were a clean beat (revenue +10% YoY to $216.4M, AI products driving 25% of net new ARR, NRR up to 97%), but the stock initially fell ~14% despite the beat before recovering on subsequent analyst price-target increases (DA Davidson to $9, UBS to $10, RBC to $9.50). The initial post-earnings selloff despite a beat, plus multiple not-clearly-dominant drivers behind the later recovery, keep this at medium rather than high; a disclosed CFO transition (Sonalee Parekh to Aziz Megji, effective March 2026) is not tied to any operational or accounting issue per the company's own filing.
invalidation: NRR growth stalls or AI-product ARR contribution flattens in the next quarterly report

thesis: Dell's rally to a fresh all-time high ($593.98) continues to be anchored in the same disclosed catalyst behind its Sept 1 Q2 FY2027 earnings: a $95B server order backlog including AI-dedicated servers, with the stock up 306% YTD and 309% over the trailing year on AI-server demand. The clearest counter-case -- 'is it too late to buy' valuation commentary and gross-margin compression as low-margin AI servers dilute the mix -- doesn't change the read given the backlog's multi-quarter revenue visibility, and no confirmed litigation, restatement, or leadership issue surfaced this run (the June 25 Texas redomestication is a routine governance change, not a disclosed problem).
invalidation: Q3 FY2027 earnings (~Nov 24) show backlog growth stalling or gross margin deteriorating further

thesis: GBTG's price sitting almost exactly at its pending $9.50/share all-cash acquisition price by Long Lake Management (shareholder vote held Aug 3, close expected H2 2026) explains both the near-52-week-high reading and the volume spike -- a merger-arbitrage ceiling and deal-related volume, not organic bullish momentum. Multiple law firms (Kaskela, Kahn Swick & Foti, Brodsky & Smith) have opened fairness investigations into the deal price and process, and the company has already supplemented its proxy disclosures to address shareholder lawsuits over alleged proxy omissions, but none has a scheduled hearing or ruling date yet.
invalidation: the merger is renegotiated, terminated, or a topping bid emerges before the expected H2 2026 close

thesis: INIO's 60-day decline (including an all-time-low close of $19.04 on Sept 1) followed Q2 2026 results that beat on EPS ($0.08 vs $0.05 est.) and showed equipment orders surging 316% YoY to a $6.6B backlog, but EBITDA margin compressed to 18.4% from 21.6% as new Data Center products carried lower average margins -- a mixed, offsetting picture rather than a clear directional read. Multiple law firms (Johnson Fistel, Schall, Kessler Topaz) are separately investigating INNIO N.V. over allegedly false or misleading statements tied to its 2026 IPO, an open, unresolved matter with no confirmed finding yet.
invalidation: would revisit if margin trends stabilize in the next quarterly report and the IPO-related investigations are resolved without a confirmed adverse finding

thesis: SPCX's 60-day gain sits alongside two unresolved, near-term overhangs: Starship Flight 14 has slipped for a third time to no earlier than Sept 22 (an unresolved binary event that could move the stock sharply either way), and September brings another wave of insider share sales as post-IPO lockups continue to unwind on a staggered schedule. Broad bullish analyst sentiment (average target near $222, Cathie Wood calling the IPO price a 'deep value opportunity') exists alongside this technical/event overhang, so the picture is mixed rather than a clear signal to treat this as a fresh long entry.
invalidation: would revisit if Starship Flight 14 succeeds and the September lockup-driven supply is absorbed without sustained price pressure
